_comment: The JUDGEMENT half of MASTER_EXECUTION_STATE.json. Everything here is an
assertion: a claim about what remains, what blocks it and what to do next.
No command produces these, so nothing here carries the authority of the
measured half. A resuming session should re-verify each item against the
measured half and against docs/exec/EXECUTION_STATUS.md before acting.
Rule for editing: an item leaves this file when its ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE
exists, not when the work feels finished. Every backlog entry therefore
carries a verification command, and an entry whose verification command
cannot be written is not yet understood well enough to be worked.

ordered_backlog.title: Extend route depth inside the admitted destinations
ordered_backlog.why_it_ranks_here: The BREADTH half is closed: 37 in scope = 19 researched + 18 assessed with evidence + 0 unexamined, and the coverage matrix now reports those two states separately instead of collapsing them. What is left is DEPTH, and it is named rather than estimated: Lebanon’s index enumerates roughly a dozen further readable routes (artist visas and artist residency, the domestic-worker entry visa, the six-month bank-statement residence visa, foreign expert at a port, religious students, Iraqi nationals, temporary residence for passport renewal); China’s guide index enumerates two more (exit-entry permits, travel permits); Türkiye enumerates subtypes its own pages do not describe.
ordered_backlog.next_action: Lebanon first — more readable routes than anywhere else in the corpus, one authority, one already-proven extraction method (by line offset out of the fetcher’s output, diffed against the mega-menu).

The four destinations added on 2026-08-26 widen the readable corpus for the first time since that measurement, so the number is worth re-running before the queue is written off — but nothing about triage effort moves it.

ordered_backlog.title: Finland is live locally and ABSENT from production, and nothing said so
ordered_backlog.why_it_ranks_here: Production publishes 13 destinations and 72 pages; the local database publishes 14 and 77. The whole difference is Finland: migri.fi challenges the VPS (BL-3), so Finland’s requirements have no source version in production and its five pages do not exist there. This was not recorded anywhere — ledger entry 30 said "87 pages in production", which was a LOCAL figure captioned as production, and the live sitemap is what settled it at 72.
ordered_backlog.next_action: Nothing in-repo. When the egress is fixed, run the sync from the VPS and Finland promotes with no new extraction work — the requirements files already exist and are already verified.

blockers.blocker: No funded OpenAI key for the eval harness

Two distinct classes, and separating them matters. (a) AUTHORITY REFUSES OUR BOT: immi.homeaffairs.gov.au, www.mofa.go.jp and france-visas.gouv.fr return 403 on robots.txt from BOTH our egress paths — policy, not IP reputation, and not fixable by engineering. (b) OUR EGRESS IS DROPPED: migri.fi challenges the VPS, and Portugal's vistos.mne.gov.pt and aima.gov.pt reset the TLS handshake from the VPS in 0.22s while answering 200 elsewhere. Class (b) is OUR infrastructure fault and is fixable.
blockers.external_input_required: For (a), nothing — the spec forbids working around bot protection. For (b), an egress those authorities do not drop: a different IP, or an allowlist via the outreach process.

next_exact_action.action: Pick the highest-ranked backlog entry whose actionable_now is true and whose verify command is defined — currently DOD-65 (route depth, Lebanon first), then DOD-11’s re-measurement against the widened corpus.
do_not: Do not rerun the whole program. Spec §0.2: resume from the first non-complete item unless evidence shows prior work is invalid.
Do not probe an authority from a laptop and treat the result as production truth. Finland passed locally and failed from the VPS.
Do not read a count out of the LOCAL database and caption it "in production". Ledger entry 30 did, and production was 15 pages and one whole country short of what it claimed.
Do not mark a backlog item complete before its acceptance evidence exists.
Do not treat a low uniqueness percentage as a verdict. It is a ratio, and a large shared menu moves the denominator — Lebanon scored in Japan’s range and is now four live routes.

standing_constraints: Never invent government data. A requirement without an official-source excerpt does not ship.
Never launder a local fetch into production. Probe from the host that will do the syncing.
A check built from the same assumption as the thing it checks will confirm it. Verify with a DIFFERENT question (B-25, B-26).
An unchecked item is not a passing one. State denominators, not just failure counts.

A landing page that fails is not a country that fails. Enumerate the site and follow the links OFF it before recording a verdict — four destinations were sitting two clicks past a page already marked `needs_deeper_research`.

Read source URLs off the site; never construct them. Kuwait 404’d a constructed URL, and its correctly-read one turned out to be empty — reading the link is what made that a finding rather than a mistake.

Do not collapse distinct failure modes into one word. An IP-level block, a client-rendered page, an unresolvable robots.txt redirect and an outright refusal are four different facts with four different futures.
